questions.question: Use calculate_correlation with method equal to pearson and use identify_clusters with n_clusters equal to 3, method equal to kmeans and use show_regression with method equal to linear in order to know How do Smoothness and Compactness measurements relate in breast cancer tumors, and what patterns distinguish benign from malignant cases?

answer.value: There is a positive relationship between Smoothness and Compactness measurements in breast cancer data. Benign tumors (357 cases) typically show lower Smoothness averaging 0.0925 (range 0.0526-0.1634) and lower Compactness averaging 0.0801 (range 0.0194-0.2239). Malignant tumors (212 cases) demonstrate higher Smoothness averaging 0.1029 (range 0.0737-0.1447) and significantly higher Compactness averaging 0.1452 (range 0.0461-0.3454). The data reveals that malignant tumors tend to cluster in the upper-right region with both higher Smoothness and Compactness values, indicating more irregular and compact tumor structures. Compactness shows a larger difference between tumor types compared to Smoothness, suggesting it may be a more discriminative feature for diagnosis.

key_insights: Malignant tumors show higher average Compactness (0.1452) compared to benign (0.0801)
Smoothness values are higher in malignant tumors (0.1029) than benign (0.0925)
Positive correlation exists between Smoothness and Compactness measurements
Malignant tumors cluster in upper-right region with high values in both dimensions
Compactness shows larger difference between tumor types than Smoothness
